newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani bourses to start depository by October.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani bourses to start depository by October.

text.p: Undeterred by current weak trading conditions, Pakistan's three bourses will switch to a central depository system (CDS) of trading by October as part of a modernisation plan, the head of one them said on Tuesday.

"The last hitch in the introduction of this system has been removed after government decided to give it the necessary legal cover in Monday's cabinet meeting," Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) president Arif Habib told Reuters in an interview.
A government statement released after a cabinet meeting on Monday said that the proposed legislation would provide a comprehensive legal framework for the effective functioning of the new system.

The sponsors of this $3.5 million project are the KSE and the Islamabad and Lahore stock exchanges, the International Finance Corporation, Citibank, Muslim Commercial Bank, Habib Bank Ltd, National Investment Trust, Investment Corporation of Pakistan, and Pakistan Industrial Credit and Investment Corp.

Habib said the Central Depository Company of Pakistan Ltd was established in 1993 to modernise trading at the Pakistani bourses. "IBM has installed the CDS hardware while its software is under trial."

"Manual handling of shares is time-consuming, needs a lot of paper work and restricts handling of large volume transactions. It is also prone to theft and forgery through counterfeit shares," he said.
"Through the central depository system, as practised in all developed markets, the operational cost will be reduced and efficiency will increase."
He said the introduction of the system would also make the Pakistani market attractive for international investors who were currently put off by physical handling of shares.
"Pakistani bourses planned a comprehensive modernisation programme in 1993 aimed to provide better services. It is now near completion", he said.
The moves followed a boom in the Pakistani market as the Karachi 100-share index peaked at a record 2,661.31 points in March 1994, mainly on foreign buying, which brought in local investors.
Brokers say the inflow of foreign funds has made it necessary for Pakistani stock exchanges to equip themselves with modern facilities.
Habib said computerised trading, which is now being done on an experimental basis, will be introduced in normal trading hours within six months.
"At present 280 companies are on computerised trading and more will be included in the list in near future."
Habib said that in the last few years, Pakistani bourses had improved their operations and the quality of brokerage services had also improved.
Now brokerage houses were coming out with regular research and analysis reports, which was not done in the past, he said.
